claims.text: Mechanical-property differences among the FCC Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni quinary alloy and its quaternary and ternary subsets are primarily governed by variations in atomic-scale short-range chemical order.
Short-range chemical order generates local lattice distortions.
The local lattice distortions associated with short-range chemical order impede dislocation glide.
Short-range chemical order modifies the energy landscape for dislocation motion.
Short-range chemical order can favor deformation twinning or other alternative deformation mechanisms.
The alternative deformation mechanisms favored by short-range chemical order enhance strain hardening.
Variations in composition and thermomechanical processing can tune the degree of short-range chemical order.
Selected quaternary and ternary subsets can be processed into single-phase FCC states through standardized thermomechanical treatments.
Alloys with enhanced short-range chemical order should have higher yield strength than the equiatomic quinary baseline.
Alloys with enhanced short-range chemical order should exhibit a more pronounced strain-hardening response than the equiatomic quinary baseline.
Stronger diffuse-scattering signals and APT cluster statistics can be used as evidence of increased short-range chemical order.
Alloys with reduced short-range chemical order have more uniform local lattice environments and fewer obstacles to dislocation motion.
Reduced short-range chemical order should produce lower yield strength than the equiatomic quinary baseline.
Reduced short-range chemical order causes earlier localization of plastic deformation.
Alloys with diminished short-range chemical order should exhibit more homogeneous deformation.
Alloys with diminished short-range chemical order should exhibit earlier strain softening.
The predicted relationships between short-range chemical order and mechanical properties should persist after accounting for stacking-fault energy and grain-boundary effects.
Controlled substitutions can connect constituent cost-performance tradeoffs to changes in local atomic interactions and microstructural state.
The proposed mechanism is limited to single-phase FCC alloys within the Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni composition family under 900–1100 K annealing and a deformation strain rate of 10^-3 s^-1.

contradictions.description: The mechanism states that reduced SRO causes earlier localization of plastic deformation, whereas the predicted outcome says diminished SRO produces more homogeneous deformation. The temporal or strain-regime distinction needed to reconcile these statements is not specified.
